hints: Start by working out what Y actually is, use the percentage data and the Mr value to find its molecular formula.
Convert each % to moles by dividing by Ar, then simplify to get the empirical formula C2H4O and scale it up using Mr = 88.0.
Think about which type of alcohol can be oxidised to a product with two oxygens, then match the carbon count back to X.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of each element in Y**

Lovely, this is a classic percentage composition job. Divide each % by the Ar to get the mole ratio.

$$\text{C}: \frac{54.54}{12.0} = 4.545 \quad \text{O}: \frac{36.36}{16.0} = 2.273 \quad \text{H}: \frac{9.10}{1.0} = 9.10$$

**Get the empirical formula**

Now divide all three numbers by the smallest to simplify. That gives you a neat whole number ratio.

$$\frac{4.545}{2.273} = 2.0 \quad \frac{2.273}{2.273} = 1.0 \quad \frac{9.10}{2.273} = 4.0$$
So the empirical formula is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ with empirical mass $= (2 \times 12) + (4 \times 1) + 16 = 44.0$.

**Find the molecular formula of Y**

Compare the empirical mass to the true Mr to find how many units join together.

$$\text{number of units} = \frac{88.0}{44.0} = 2$$
So molecular formula of Y $= \text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$.

**Link Y back to alcohol X**

A product with formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ containing two oxygens formed by oxidation of an alcohol must be a carboxylic acid. Only a primary alcohol oxidises all the way to a carboxylic acid with the same carbon number.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
That is butan-1-ol oxidised to butanoic acid, which matches option C.

options.A: This is butan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. It oxidises to the ketone butanone, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$, which has only one oxygen and Mr = 72, not $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$.
options.B: This is pentan-1-ol with 5 carbons. Full oxidation would give pentanoic acid, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$ with Mr = 102, too heavy for Y with Mr = 88.0.
options.C: This is butan-1-ol, a primary alcohol with 4 carbons. It can be oxidised first to butanal then to butanoic acid, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ with Mr = 88.0, exactly matching the analysis of Y.
options.D: This is pentan-3-ol, a secondary alcohol with 5 carbons. It oxidises to the ketone pentan-3-one, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$, which has the wrong formula and wrong Mr.
